zh.summary: Opio 是面向交易服务团队的金融尽职调查 AI 平台，以总账为起点，把数据室文档转化为可追溯的 FDD 分析、数据簿与调整建议。
zh.judgment: 最关键的商业判断是：在高度依赖专业判断与审计留痕的 FDD 场景，卖点不是通用模型能力，而是把事务所既有方法、控制与复核流程封装成可部署的工作流；能否规模化取决于交付与合规成本，而非模型本身。
zh.replaces: 替代交易服务团队在数据室中逐份阅读文档、手工搭建 trial balance 与 databook、逐项寻找 EBITDA 与净债务调整依据的重复准备工作，以及部分通用文档 AI 工具的事后拼接流程。
zh.segment: 面向并购与交易咨询的金融尽职调查（FDD）垂直 AI 工作流
zh.product: Opio 的产品范围围绕一次完整 FDD 业务展开：从数据室进入、总账与试算平衡表处理，到 databook 生成和 EBITDA、净债务调整建议。公司称其专用 agent 会在数据室落地后即开始阅读全部文档并产出各项分析的初稿，每个数字可回溯至总账，每一步要么通过要么升级人工复核。平台强调按事务所自身的科目映射、databook 格式和控制规则进行配置，而非强推统一方法。官网未提供文档、API 或具体功能清单，因此上述能力范围只能视为公司披露，尚缺独立验证。
zh.customer: 使用者是交易服务团队中的 FDD 专业人员，包括四大之外的大型审计与咨询网络及独立事务所的分析师、经理与合伙人；付费方通常是事务所或交易咨询部门，而非单个交易客户。痛点是每个项目数据室文档量大、时间窗口紧、复核标准高，重复的数据整理挤占了判断与客户沟通时间。官网客户故事提到 Forvis Mazars 与 BDO France，说明其目标客户是具备跨国交付能力的中大型专业服务机构；但客户数量、合同规模与续约情况均未披露。
zh.workflow: 输入是交易数据室中的财务与业务文档，核心是总账和试算平衡表；平台读取文档与账目至分录层级，生成 databook 初稿，并就发现的 EBITDA 与净债务调整逐项给出支持证据。专业人员在此基础上审阅、修改并形成结论，控制机制决定哪些步骤自动通过、哪些升级复核。官网引用的一位 Nexia 经理案例是从 391 份文档重建完整开票数据库，属于单点任务示例，尚不足以证明端到端报告交付的完整覆盖。
zh.business_model: 已知信息未披露定价方式、计费单位（按席位、按项目还是按部署）或合同期限，因此无法判断单位经济。可合理推断（非公司披露）其销售是面向事务所的企业级部署，涉及安全审查、IT 集成与本地化配置，获客周期长、前期实施成本高，收入更可能来自年度订阅加部署服务。由于缺少定价页与文档，无法核实是否存在试用、按用量计费或分层套餐。
zh.traction: 公司披露的采用信号包括：平均每个 FDD 项目节省 27% 时间、覆盖 15 个国家与 4 大洲、累计分析超过 100 万份文档；Forvis Mazars 在九个月试点后于 10 个国家部署，BDO France 也有客户故事。这些均为公司自述，未经审计，且“节省时间”缺少基线定义。缺失的关键证据包括付费客户数、收入、留存与扩展率、单项目使用频次，以及客户是否在无试点补贴下续约。
zh.moat: 与通用大模型相比，Opio 的差异在于从总账出发的可追溯性、内置的通过/升级控制、按事务所方法配置的能力，以及支持本地化甚至本地部署的安全架构。这些特性贴合 FDD 对审计留痕与保密的要求，构成一定的流程与信任壁垒。但壁垒并非不可逾越：通用模型厂商可向上封装工作流，四大内部平台也可能自建；只有当 Opio 持续积累行业方法模板、通过客户安全审查并形成切换成本时，优势才可持续。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 400 万欧元融资，投资方包括 Frst、Seedcamp 与 Global Founders Capital；轮次在数据中被标为 Other，不能据此推断为种子轮或 A 轮，投资方名单也不等于领投名单。该金额说明机构愿意支持其早期商业化，但资金用途未披露，无法判断是投向产品、交付团队还是市场扩张。下一里程碑应是可验证的付费客户扩展与跨国家部署的可复制性，而非更多试点。
zh.risks: 首要失败条件是交付不可规模化：每个事务所都要求定制科目映射、部署环境与安全审查，若实施成本随客户数线性上升，毛利与扩张速度都会受限。其次是信任与责任风险：若 AI 建议的调整出现错误而复核未能拦截，可能引发专业责任与客户流失；此外，通用模型或事务所自建平台可能压缩其差异化空间。监管对 AI 在审计与交易服务中的使用要求趋严，也会拉长销售周期。
zh.takeaway: 对垂直 AI 创业者而言，Opio 的可借鉴之处是选择一个判断密集、留痕要求高、通用工具难以直接落地的专业流程，把“人在回路”的控制设计成产品的一部分，而不是事后补丁；同时以事务所自身方法为配置对象，降低采用阻力。
zh.watch_next: 下一步应观察：是否公开定价与部署模式、付费客户数与续约率是否披露、27% 时间节省是否有可复核的基线，以及 Forvis Mazars 的 10 国部署能否扩展为更多国家与更多业务线。

en.summary: Opio is an AI platform for transaction services that starts from the general ledger and turns data-room documents into traceable financial due diligence analysis, databooks and adjustment suggestions.
en.judgment: The key commercial question is whether Opio can sell workflow, controls and auditability rather than generic model capability in a judgment-heavy FDD market; scale will depend on delivery and compliance costs, not on the model itself.
en.replaces: It replaces manual document review in data rooms, hand-built trial balances and databooks, and the search for supporting evidence behind EBITDA and net-debt adjustments, as well as generic document-AI tools retrofitted to finance.
en.segment: Vertical AI workflow for financial due diligence in M&A and transaction advisory
en.product: Opio's scope follows a full FDD engagement: data-room intake, general-ledger and trial-balance processing, databook generation, and suggested EBITDA and net-debt adjustments. The company says specialised agents begin reading every document as soon as the data room lands and produce a first cut of each analysis, with every figure reconciling back to the ledger and every step either passing or escalating to human review. The platform is configured to a firm's own chart-of-accounts mapping, databook formats and controls rather than imposing one method. No documentation, API reference or detailed feature list was retrieved, so these capabilities remain company-reported and unverified.
en.customer: Users are FDD professionals in transaction services teams, including analysts, managers and partners at large audit and advisory networks and independent firms; the buyer is typically the firm or transaction advisory practice, not an individual deal client. The pain is high document volume, tight deal timelines and strict review standards, with repetitive data preparation crowding out judgment and client dialogue. Customer stories name Forvis Mazars and BDO France, suggesting mid-to-large professional-services firms with cross-border delivery; client counts, contract sizes and renewals are not disclosed.
en.workflow: Inputs are financial and business documents in the deal data room, centred on the general ledger and trial balance. Opio reads documents and accounts down to entry level, drafts the databook, and proposes EBITDA and net-debt adjustments each with supporting evidence. Professionals then review, shape and conclude, while built-in controls decide which steps pass automatically and which escalate. A cited Nexia manager example rebuilt a complete invoicing database from 391 documents, a single-task illustration that does not yet prove end-to-end report delivery.
en.business_model: Pricing, billing unit (seat, project or deployment) and contract terms are not disclosed, so unit economics cannot be assessed. A reasonable inference, not a company statement, is enterprise sales to firms with security review, IT integration and local configuration, implying long sales cycles and high implementation cost, with revenue likely from annual subscriptions plus deployment services. The absence of a pricing page and documentation means trials, usage-based pricing or tiered plans cannot be confirmed.
en.traction: Company-reported adoption signals include 27% average time saved per FDD, 15 countries and 4 continents served, and over 1 million documents analysed. Forvis Mazars deployed across 10 countries after a nine-month pilot, and BDO France has a customer story. These are self-reported and unaudited, and the time-saving figure lacks a defined baseline. Missing evidence includes paying customer counts, revenue, retention and expansion rates, per-engagement usage, and whether clients renew without pilot subsidies.
en.moat: Versus general-purpose models, Opio's differentiation is ledger-anchored traceability, built-in pass/escalate controls, configuration to a firm's own method, and a security architecture supporting localised or on-premise deployment. These fit FDD's audit-trail and confidentiality requirements and create process and trust barriers. They are not insurmountable: model vendors can package workflows upward and the Big Four can build internally; the advantage holds only if Opio keeps accumulating method templates, clears client security reviews and creates switching costs.
en.funding_read: The round is EUR 4 million with Frst, Seedcamp and Global Founders Capital listed as investors; the dataset labels the stage as Other, so it should not be read as seed or Series A, and the investor list is not a lead-investor list. The amount signals institutional support for early commercialisation, but use of funds is undisclosed, so allocation to product, delivery or go-to-market is unknown. The next milestone should be verifiable paying-customer expansion and repeatable multi-country deployment, not more pilots.
en.risks: The first failure condition is non-scalable delivery: if every firm requires custom account mapping, deployment environments and security review, implementation cost rises with each client and margins and expansion slow. The second is trust and liability: an erroneous AI adjustment that review fails to catch could trigger professional-liability and churn issues, while general models or in-house firm platforms could erode differentiation. Tightening regulation of AI in audit and transaction services would also lengthen sales cycles.
en.takeaway: For vertical AI founders, Opio's lesson is to pick a judgment-dense, audit-heavy professional workflow that generic tools cannot easily land, and design human-in-the-loop controls into the product rather than bolting them on; configuring to the firm's own method lowers adoption friction.
en.watch_next: Watch whether Opio publishes pricing and deployment models, discloses paying customers and renewal rates, provides a reviewable baseline for the 27% time saving, and extends the Forvis Mazars 10-country deployment to more countries and service lines.

Opio Product Security Company Customers Book a demo CUSTOMER STORY Forvis Mazars Across markets and data rooms: how Forvis Mazars Group is scaling agentic AI Interviewed Pierre-Paul Jacquet Deal Advisory at Forvis Mazars Grégory Volpi Partner Transaction Services at Forvis Mazars Share this customer story Deployed across 10 countries, Opio is helping Forvis Mazars Group (“Forvis Mazars”) bring specialised, secure agentic AI into the everyday work of international transaction services teams. Transaction Services across borders Forvis Mazars Group, the international leader in audit and assurance, tax and advisory services, helps clients prepare for what’s next by combining international scale and reach with local market expertise. In Transaction Services, that means bringing together teams that understand the financial, operational and cultural realities of each market while maintaining consistently high standards and delivering seamless collaboration across an engagement. Grégory Volpi has more than twenty years of financial due diligence experience, including transactions across Europe, North America, Africa and Asia. Pierre-Paul Jacquet began his career in Paris and now advises on global transactions from his base in London. Having been involved in over 200 deals on the buy and sell side globally for corporates and investors, he also set up and led the Group's Financial Advisory practice across Asia-Pacific from Singapore. Their experience reflects a central reality of international transaction services: local environments vary, but clients expect the same support, quality and professional judgement wherever a transaction takes place. "London is one of the world's most international deal markets. Our teams need technology that can support the same standard of analysis across businesses, reporting environments and jurisdictions. Opio was built for that reality." PIERRE-PAUL JACQUET One specialised approach, across 10 countries Forvis Mazars has now deployed Opio across 10 countries, as a GenAI-powered solution to transform transaction advisory services and due diligence. This breadth demonstrates that the platform is not tied to a single jurisdiction, accounting environment or way of organising transaction services. Each market retains its local expertise and professional judgement, while teams share a specialised approach to bringing agentic AI into their work. For an international organisation, this matters. Innovation needs to travel across borders without imposing one country's operating model on another. A platform must be flexible enough to work within local requirements while maintaining a consistent level of quality, reviewability and control worldwide. The team worked with Forvis Mazars to ensure deep domain alignment, embedded controls and humanintheloop review capability – streamlining complex workflows while preserving professional judgment. This deployment, currently across 10 countries, gives Forvis Mazars a common foundation for adoption, while enabling each team to apply the technology to the realities and requirements of its own market and engagements. From experimentation to adoption Forvis Mazars views artificial intelligence as part of a broader transformation of professional services. The opportunity is not simply to provide teams with another tool. It is to embed new ways of working into the processes where technology can create meaningful value. Before adopting Opio more broadly, Forvis Mazars conducted a nine-month pilot to test the platform from end to end. The pilot assessed more than the quality of individual outputs. It examined how Opio fitted into Transaction Services team workflows, how professionals reviewed its work, how teams adopted it and how it could be deployed securely across the organisation. Opio worked alongside the Forvis Mazars’ AI team throughout this process. Transaction Services professionals identified the workflows that mattered. The AI team helped create the conditions for responsible adoption. Opio contributed technology and expertise focused specifically on the mechanics of the profession. Together, they helped teams learn how to frame work for specialised agents, provide the right context, review the supporting evidence and decide when an analysis needed to go further. "Adoption happens when the technology fits the reality of the engagement. Our work with Opio and our AI team is about helping people understand where agentic AI adds value, how to use it responsibly and how it can strengthen the quality of their work." GRÉGORY VOLPI Security as a foundation for scale Responsible AI and security was a core requirement defined by Forvis Mazars in the selection and deployment of Opio. It was considered from the beginning of the pilot, not added as a final technical review. Opio worked closely with Forvis Mazars IT teams to understand their requirements and prepare deployments adapted to the firm's infrastructure and governance standards. All outputs are subject to mandatory professional review, ensuring accountability, transparency and human oversight. The solution operates exclusively on secure client data rooms, does not train on client data and preserves strict confidentiality. Forvis Mazars wanted to ensure full traceability, with clear audit trails linking outputs to source documents. This ensured the essential compliance with data protection regulations, internal AI governance and professional standards, mitigating bias and operational risk by design rather than after deployment. Opio was also able to be deployed on premise, giving Forvis Mazars greater control of where sensitive information is processed and how the platform fits within its technology environment. This flexibility is critical for an international organisation. Local requirements may vary, but every deployment must provide the confidence required for teams to use the technology on live engagements. "Security was a major criterion from the start. Opio worked through our IT requirements and could support an on-premise deployment, giving us the confidence to move from a nine-month pilot to broader adoption." GRÉGORY VOLPI Why Forvis Mazars chose Opio Forvis Mazars was not looking for a general-purpose AI platform. It needed a specialist that understood Transaction Services, could operate across an international organisation and could meet the professional, IT and legal standards required for deployment. Opio's focus on the profession made that possible. Its team understood the workflows and level of scrutiny required on a live transaction. The platform passed the firm's business, IT and legal review, while its deployment model could be adapted to the security and infrastructure requirements of different countries. Deploying Opio across financial advisory engagements has streamlined transaction and accounting review workflows. Overall, this solution reduces manual document review, accelerates due diligence timelines and improves consistency across complex engagements. Its advisors can spend more time on professional judgment, risk assessment and client dialogue rather than data processing. Clients benefit from faster deal execution, clearer financial insights and an improved experience in timecritical transactions. The result is a solution designed not only to introduce agentic AI, but to make it usable, trusted and relevant in the everyday work of international deal teams.
